The alloy was prepared by permanent mold direct-chill casting [31]. Alloy melt was kept at 720 ◦C for 20 min in a cylinder steel crucible. Then the melt-containing crucible was immerged into the cooling water at a speed of 40 mm min−1, then the ingot with a diameter of 60 mm and length of 140 mm was prepared.

The rod billet with a diameter of 43 mm and height of 35 mm was cut from the ingot, then indirect-extruded at 350 ◦C and 400 ◦C, respectively, under a ram speed of 0.1 mm s−1 and an extrusion ratio of 12. The billet was hold at extrusion temperature for 10 min prior to extrusion.

The results indicate that W phase (Mg3Y2Zn3) is the main intermetallic compound in the alloy.

evidence.quote: The particle bands in the alloy extruded at 400 ◦C are distributed more homogeneously than those in the alloy extruded at 350 ◦C.

attributes.location: propagates through DRXed and unDRXed areas

evidence.quote: In the alloy extruded at 350 ◦C (Fig. 10(a)), a long crack with more than 200 μm in length is observed to propagate through the DRXed and unDRXed areas.
While in the alloy extruded at 400 ◦C, many small cracks with 10 μm in length are initiated at different locations of particle bands, as shown in Fig. 10(b).
